title: How a Snowdrift Becomes an Igloo
script: If you're stuck in a blizzard with the sun going down, and you dig a hole in a snowdrift, you have an igloo. But by midnight the roof sags onto your face, because loose snow can't hold itself up, so you climb out, find hard wind-packed snow, and saw it into blocks. But a straight wall of blocks just leans in and falls, so you lay them in a rising spiral, each block leaning on the one before it, and the ring closes itself into a dome with no scaffolding at all. This is a spiral dome. But now it's sealed so tight that your own breath has nowhere to go and the air turns stale, so you poke a fist-sized hole in the top. This is a vent. But the wind blows straight through your doorway and steals your heat, so you dig the entrance lower than the floor, because cold air is heavy and sinks. This is a cold trap, and that is why an igloo's door is a tunnel. But you're still lying where the cold collects, so you pile a snow shelf high at the back, where the warm air rises. But your body heat starts the walls dripping on you all night, so you light a seal oil lamp, let the inside surface melt, and it refreezes into a hard shell of ice. This is a qulliq. Now it can be minus forty outside, and warm enough up on your shelf to sleep. Add loose snow in the gaps, a block for a door, and caribou skins on the walls. Congratulations, you have built an igloo.
